headline: Bitcoin holds near $73,700 as Wall Street banks back a $270M stablecoin venture and ETF outflows hit day four
summary: Bitcoin barely moved Wednesday, hovering around $73,700 while spot ETF outflows stretched into a fourth consecutive session — a sign that institutional selling pressure hasn't let up. The bigger story was off-chain: Goldman Sachs, Citi, and other major banks are reportedly committing $270 million to a new stablecoin venture, and Deutsche Bank went live with a digital asset custody service. Traditional finance is deepening its crypto footprint even as the Fear & Greed index sits at 29, firmly in fear territory.

winners.name: Gram (prev. Toncoin)
winners.catalyst: No single confirmed catalyst; the broader tokenization narrative and renewed institutional interest in blockchain infrastructure appear to have lifted sentiment around the rebranded asset.

losers.name: Zcash
losers.catalyst: No Zcash-specific news drove the drop; continued regulatory pressure on privacy coins and a risk-off market (Fear & Greed at 29) weighed heavily, with capital appearing to rotate into Monero (+5.8%) rather than exit privacy coins entirely.

whyItMoved:
Bitcoin's near-flat session masks a meaningful undercurrent: spot BTC ETFs recorded outflows for the fourth straight day, meaning institutional fund redemptions have been a persistent drag even as AI and tech stocks bounced. When ETFs see sustained outflows, it typically reflects fund managers and retail investors pulling money out of Bitcoin-linked products — and four consecutive days of that is a signal worth watching, even if each individual day's move looks small.

The Fear & Greed index at 29 — deep in fear territory — tells the same story. The market isn't panicking, but it isn't buying either.

Meanwhile, Bitcoin Core developers disclosed three previously patched security vulnerabilities, including one rated high-severity that affected mining. The flaws are already fixed, so there's no active risk, but disclosures like this can briefly shake confidence, particularly in a market already leaning cautious.

Zcash's 15% drop stands out in the top 15. No specific news triggered it, but privacy-focused coins have faced sustained regulatory scrutiny, and in a risk-off environment they tend to get hit harder. Monero's 5.8% gain on the same day suggests some traders rotated between the two privacy coins rather than exiting the category entirely. Gram's 14.8% surge — the day's biggest winner — had no clear single catalyst; the rebranded asset (formerly Toncoin) appears to have caught a bid amid broader tokenization enthusiasm.
worthKnowing: Goldman Sachs, Citi, and other major Wall Street banks are reportedly committing $270 million to a new stablecoin venture, one of the largest traditional-finance bets on crypto infrastructure to date.
Deutsche Bank went live with its digital asset custody service and signed an asset management partnership, marking a direct step into crypto market infrastructure for one of Europe's largest banks.
Bitcoin Core developers disclosed three patched vulnerabilities — including a high-severity mining bug — as part of a responsible disclosure process; no active exploit risk remains.
OKXICE confirmed a November 23 launch for its tokenized stock trading platform, which will list Strategy, Coinbase, and Circle shares under an SEC innovation exemption.
